title: Core a trimmed cabbage half: cut along both sides of the core to its tip, pull the core out, leave the leaves stacked
instruction: Cut the pale core out of the cabbage half with the knife, set the core on the board, put the knife down, and leave the green leaves stacked in place.
context: Food preparation workers cut and trim vegetables every shift (O*NET 35-2021.00), and cabbage is cored before it is sliced. Two knife cuts must follow the pale core's outline down to the board and meet at its tip: cutting wide wastes leaves, cutting narrow leaves hard core behind. The freed core is then drawn out through the root end without dragging the loose leaf layers with it.
setup: Station bench, top z=0.7475 m; x away from the robot, y to its left. OXO Good Grips 11272900 polypropylene cutting board, 535.9 x 368.3 x 20 mm, fixed, centre (0.52, 0), top z=0.7675. Green cabbage half, cut face up, trimmed to a 140 x 76 x 60 mm centre strip, 300 g: three stacked green leaf layers (85 g each) around a pale core (45 g) whose outline is a triangle 50 mm wide at the root face and 40 mm long to its tip, modelled 58 mm high; root end toward the robot, the core's base exposed there. Mercer Millennia M23850 boning knife: 152 x 21 x 1.8 mm steel blade, black 128 x 30 x 30 mm handle, 140 g (handle size and mass estimated), lying flat, blade pointing +x. Steel ruler 200 x 12 x 2 mm, 10 mm ticks, at (0.35, 0.175). Lot A: cabbage centre (0.330, 0.070), square; knife handle centre (0.330, -0.135, 0.7835). Lot B: cabbage (0.320, 0.075) turned 15 degrees counter-clockwise; knife (0.330, -0.100, 0.7835). No jitter. Screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Score 0 for the trial if at any moment the blade touches a gripper; the blade comes within 30 mm of the gripper not holding the knife by its handle; the core moves more than 15 mm relative to the leaves before both sides of its outline are cut; or the knife cuts more than 25 mm into the leaves beyond the outline. Otherwise judged at the end, with both grippers at least 5 mm clear of cabbage and knife, knife, core and bottom layer on the board, and all still (under 1 mm) for 1 s; if not, 0. 1.0 if the core is out, at least 10 mm from every leaf, every leaf layer within 10 mm of where it started, the cuts ran at most 5 mm outside the outline into the leaves, and no core piece over 10 mm long is left on the leaves; 0.67 as 1.0 but cuts up to 10 mm into the leaves or a core piece over 10 mm left; 0.33 for at least one knife cut along the outline (2 mm inside to 10 mm outside it) at least 20 mm long and 5 mm deep, also the most if a leaf layer ends over 10 mm from its start; 0 otherwise. A cut counts only with the knife held by its handle and its edge leading (drawn or pushed edge first, within 45 degrees of the blade plane). Real trial: top photos with the ruler before and after, ruler on the removed piece (green strip width) and on any pale core over 2 mm thick left on the leaves, video stepped frame by frame for cuts and clearances. Lots A and B averaged.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (120 s at 20 Hz) per trial
reset_notes: Each real trial uses a fresh green head cabbage (1.5-2.5 kg, 160-190 mm across): halve through the stem, cut a 76 mm centre strip, slice it 60 mm thick and 140 mm long; keep 250-350 g strips whose pale core triangle is 35-55 mm wide and 30-60 mm long; weigh and photograph it. Wash the knife by hand, clean the board, fit new cut-resistant pad covers. In simulation each trial resets the half whole (joints restored) and the knife to the lot's pose.
fidelity: True size. The half is 4 rigid bodies (3 stacked 85 g leaf layers, 45 g full-height core) joined by fixed joints. PhysX cannot cut; the knife passes through with no force, so nothing needs steadying. An outline point is cut when the held blade's leading edge sweeps it, 2 mm inside to 10 mm outside; at 98% of both sides the core is freed. Edge motion up to 45 degrees off the blade plane counts (the demo's is 30); a real blade drifts toward its plane, so real trials judge where cuts end.
scores: Scripted demo: 1.0 (lot A 1.0, lot B 1.0). Dream-1 run: 0.0 (lot A 0.0, lot B 0.0; both reached the step limit; in lot A the arms pulled back and never touched the knife or cabbage).
